v.2: "Truly I know that it is so, But how can man be just with God?
v.3: If he is pleased to contend with him, He can't answer him one time in a thousand.
v.4: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: Who has hardened himself against him, and prospered?
v.5: Who removes the mountains, and they don't know it, When he overturns them in his anger
v.6: Who shakes the earth out of its place; The pillars of it tremble;
v.7: Who commands the sun, and it doesn't rise, And seals up the stars;
v.8: Who alone stretches out the heavens, Treads on the waves of the sea;
v.9: Who makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, And the chambers of the south;
v.10: Who does great things past finding out, Yes, marvelous things without number.
v.11: Behold, he goes by me, and I don't see him. He passes on also, but I don't perceive him.
v.12: Behold, he snatches away; who can hinder him? Who will ask him, 'What are you doing?'
v.13: "God will not withdraw his anger; The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.
v.14: How much less shall I answer him, Choose my words to argue with him?
v.15: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer. I would make supplication to my judge.
v.16: If I had called, and he had answered me, Yet would I not believe that he listened to my voice.
v.17: For he breaks me with a tempest, Multiplies my wounds without cause.
v.18: He will not allow me to take my breath, But fills me with bitterness.
v.19: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, 'Who,' says he, 'will summon me?'
v.20: Though I am righteous, my own mouth shall condemn me. Though I am blameless, it shall prove me perverse.
v.21: I am blameless. I don't regard myself. I despise my life.
v.22: "It is all the same. Therefore I say, He destroys the blameless and the wicked.
v.23: If the scourge kills suddenly, He will mock at the trial of the innocent.
v.24: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of the judges of it. If not he, then who is it?
v.25: "Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away, they see no good,
v.26: They have passed away as the swift ships, As the eagle that swoops on the prey.
v.27: If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;'
v.28: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent.
v.29: I shall be condemned; Why then do I labor in vain?
v.30: If I wash myself with snow, And cleanse my hands with lye,
v.31: Yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes shall abhor me.
v.32: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, That we should come together in judgment.
v.33: There is no umpire between us, That might lay his hand on us both.
v.34: Let him take his rod away from me, Let his terror not make me afraid:
v.35: Then I would speak, and not fear him, For I am not so in myself.
